advice: Experiment: pack each 2VL-wide column panel of B into contiguous k-major storage, with each reduction row containing the panel's columns. Reuse that packed panel across row tiles. Keep the existing four ZA accumulators and increasing-k FP32 MOPA updates; do not change the transpose of A or the general gemm ABI. Allocate and fill the panel buffer inside gemm so setup cost stays in the timed call. Hypothesis: contiguous, compact B loads may reduce address and cache costs in the SME consumer enough to offset packing. This is unverified advice, not a measured fact.
risks: Packing adds a full read and write of B for each panel and may cost more than it saves. A packed panel may also displace A or output data from cache. Do not infer a gain from historical battery scores or attribute any joint result to this experiment alone.
